newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita develops high-storage video discs.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita develops high-storage video discs.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. Ltd. said Monday it had developed technology to produce high-definition digital video discs (DVDs) with more than five times the storage capacity of standard DVDs.
The new technology can produce discs capable of holding 15 gigabytes of data on each side, while current rewriteable DVDs can store only 2.6 gigabytes per side, a Matsushita Electric official said.

Matsushita, whose products are sold under the National and Panasonic brands, is one of a host of electronics companies working on computer and entertainment equipment offering expanded storage capacity.
Last month, Sony Corp. announced it had developed technology to produce recordable optical discs able to store 12 gigabytes of information on a single side, using a high-power blue-green laser.
Matsushita's method uses a 15-milliwatt second harmonic generation (SHG) blue laser.
Matsushita said it had not yet set a date for commercial production of the discs.
